decisions.rationale: tailnum has distinct_count 3322 equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so one row per aircraft tail number is the defensible grain.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across 3322 rows, so no exact duplicates exist in bronze and no dedupe step is applied.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata and carry only capture-tool state, so they are dropped.
year, engines, seats, and speed landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but every profiled value is integral, so they are cast to INTEGER.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null) but the 13 populated values are valid speeds (90 to 432), so the column is retained with nulls preserved rather than dropped or imputed.
year has 70 nulls (null_rate 0.021072); nulls are retained as unknown manufacture years rather than imputed or failed.

purpose: silver_nyc_planes is the cleaned aircraft dimension derived from bronze.nyc_planes, providing one row per aircraft tail number with manufacturer, model, type, engine, seat, and performance attributes for joining to flight-level fact tables.
usage: Join on tailnum, which is unique and non-null at this grain. Count columns (year_manufactured, engines, seats, speed) are cast to INTEGER from landed decimals. Consumers relying on speed must handle nulls deliberately, as it is populated for fewer than 1% of aircraft; year_manufactured is also nullable for about 2% of rows.
limitations: The speed column is sparsely populated (null_rate 0.993076) and retained as-is; no imputation was performed. year_manufactured is null for 70 aircraft (null_rate 0.021072). Airbyte capture columns were dropped, so bronze lineage identifiers are not available in this table. Grain uniqueness on tailnum is asserted from profile evidence (distinct_count 3322 of 3322 rows) and should be verified against the warehouse before approval.
